chunks: From him, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be made your ransom. It has been narrated from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام regarding a sick person who remains unconscious for several days. Some of them said: he makes up the salat (prayer) of the day in which he regained consciousness; and some said: he makes up the salat (prayer) of three days and leaves what is beyond that; and some said: there is no make-up upon him. So he wrote: he makes up the salat (prayer) of the day in which he regains consciousness.
Thus, the proper way to understand these reports is what we mentioned first: that it is on the basis of recommendation and desirability, not obligation and requirement.

key_terms.النَّدْبِ: desirability or encouragement in legal valuation
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommended status rather than binding duty
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer to be made up
key_terms.يَقْضِي: to make up missed ritual acts, here missed salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُغْمَى: to be rendered unconscious or lose awareness
key_terms.يُفِيقُ: to regain consciousness or recover awareness

ai.seo_question: Does an unconscious sick person have to make up missed salat (prayer) after regaining consciousness?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a sick person who was unconscious for several days and then regains consciousness. It presents differing transmitted views about whether missed salat (prayer) must be made up, then states that he makes up the salat (prayer) of the day in which he recovers, while the concluding note explains that such reports are to be understood as recommending this act rather than making it strictly obligatory.
